answer: Each seat leases a numbered dark-sky post and is issued a goose quill plus a book of yarrow paper whose watermark serial binds it to that post. Every epoch it must ink a sketch of an assigned nebula field with the star's current altitude, then photograph the page. Haze and turbulence are local and unrepeatable, so sketches cannot be pre-generated: two seats under one sky show identical seeing and both fail. A sybil farmer must rent a thousand posts, register a thousand quills, buy a thousand serialized books and keep a thousand observers awake on clear nights. Cost scales linearly.
